chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Aasim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the man who returns from a journey during the month of Ramadan, and enters to his family when it is morning, or when the day has risen. He (peace be upon him) said: 'When the dawn emerges and he is outside and has not yet entered to his family, he is with the choice: if he wills, he fasts, and if he wills, he breaks [the fast].'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a traveler returning home during Ramadan if dawn breaks before he enters his house?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the status of a traveler returning home during Ramadan, establishing that if dawn breaks while he is still outside and has not yet entered his home or consummated relations, he retains the discretionary choice (al-khiyar) to fast or break his fast. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic view that the obligation of fasting becomes binding only upon the specific conditions of residence and intent being met at the time of Fajr, offering flexibility for those in transit. It underscores the practical ease (taysir) granted to travelers in Shia fiqh, distinguishing their status from residents who must fast once dawn is clearly established.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Nazar Bin Suweyd, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,

‘I asked Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> about the man who comes back from a journey during a Month of Ramazan, so he comes over to his family when it is morning, or the day has risen. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When the dawn emerges and he is outside and has not yet come over to his family, so he is with the choice, if he so desires to, he Fasts, and if he so desires to, he breaks’.
en.sarwar: 6. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from ‘Asem ibn Hamid from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following:

“I once asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who comes from his journey and arrives in his family when it is morning and the day is high. He (the Imam) said, ‘If it is dawn and he is not yet arrived in his family, then he has the choice to fast or not to fast.’”
